title: First instruments and learning to read in Chicago
summary: He started on guitar and mandolin with his brother, settled on bass, had no lessons until Chicago and studied with Dave Jackson.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Well can you tell us, when you first took up music, did you start on bass or any other instrument? What was your first instrument? Guitar. Oh yeah.

I was messing around with my brother, had all the minstrels laying around and I used to play a few little numbers on the mandolin, you know. I liked guitar, you know, for a while, but it always was for me to be a bass player. Did you take any lessons on it or did he show you? He did. I didn't take any kind of lessons. I just picked it up, you understand, and with him showing me. I didn't take no kind of lessons until I got to Chicago. I didn't know nothing about that.
About reading music until you got to Chicago.
In Chicago and I had an old man Jackson. Dave Payton's a man that told me, you go to Dave Jackson and take you some lessons. Well he used to have the band in the Grand Theater.
Oh yes, I knew some of the people that studied with him too. How old were you when you started on the guitar, would you say?
In fact, when I started out, I was around nine years old. When did you have a bass? I really was around ten years old. I was playing a little bass. Already on bass?
